title: [18/10/2025] - Australian marriage trends across four decades
prompt: The table below gives information about the situation of marriage and age from 1960 to 2000 in Australia. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates changes in the numbers of religious and civil marriages, as well as the average ages of brides and grooms in Australia over a 40-year period from 1960 to 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while civil marriages and the average ages of both brides and grooms all rose steadily throughout the period, the number of religious marriages fluctuated. In addition, by the end of the period, civil marriages had surpassed religious ceremonies to become the more common form of marriage.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding marriage types, in 1960, there were 25,000 religious marriages, which was over three times higher than the figure for civil marriages, at just 8,000. Over the following decades, civil marriages experienced consistent growth, rising to 12,000 in 1970, then 16,000 in 1980, before increasing more sharply to 23,000 in 1990 and ultimately reaching 40,000 by 2000, representing a fivefold increase overall. In contrast, religious marriages showed a more volatile pattern, rising initially to 28,000 in 1970 and peaking at 50,000 in 1980, before plummeting to 32,000 in 1990 and then recovering slightly to 34,000 at the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the ages at marriage, in 1960, brides were on average 21 years old, while grooms were 24, a gap of three years. The average age of brides then increased steadily throughout the period, rising by two years each decade to reach 23 in 1970, 25 in 1980, and 27 in 1990, before finally reaching 30 in 2000. Similarly, the average age of grooms also climbed progressively from 24 in 1960 to 25 in 1970, 27 in 1980, 30 in 1990, and ultimately 32 by 2000, though the age gap between spouses had narrowed slightly to two years by the final year.
